### REQ-028: Device-level rooms-set must merge, not clobber; device routes must survive a rooms rebuild

- **Status:** DONE
- **Added:** 2026-07-04
- **Completed:** 2026-07-04
- **Verified by:** live run on bench device GIMYB (Rev B), 2026-07-04 —
  `thermoctl test --suite functional` checks `f.devset.merge`,
  `f.devset.membership`, `f.devset.routes` pass, plus full suite 42/42;
  boot path unchanged (device loads stored config, answers `get` after
  reboot, no duplicate device routes)
- **Depends on:** REQ-003, REQ-008, REQ-009; found by REQ-027's suite on bench device GIMYB
- **Description:**

  Two defects in the handling of `cmd/<deviceId>/set` payloads containing a
  `rooms` array, found live on 2026-07-04:

  **Bug A — wholesale replace instead of merge (also present in legacy 0.6.4).**
  `Thermo::processJsonAsObj` does `rooms_.clear()` and rebuilds every room
  from the payload object alone. A partial payload like
  `{"rooms":[{"name":"x","currentTarget":19}]}` therefore silently (1) deletes
  all other rooms and (2) resets room `x` to factory defaults + the one field
  — including its actuator **channels**. This clobbered live device 7ROBA
  (3 rooms → 1 default room driving the wrong valves); config was restored
  from thermoctl's inventory cache the same day. `doc/MQTT.md` promised merge
  semantics ("possible to only [set], multiple or all values in one command").

  **Bug B — device-level cmd routes lost (ESP-IDF port only).**
  The rebuild calls `MqttRouter::unsubscribeAll()`, which *discards* the whole
  routing table. New rooms re-register their routes, but the device-level
  `cmd/<id>/set|get` routes registered once in `Thermo::subscribe()` are gone
  until reboot — the device becomes unmanageable over MQTT, and since the
  clobbered config was persisted, the damage survives the reboot.

  **Fix (agreed semantics):**
  - `cmd/<deviceId>/set` with `rooms[]` = **deployment semantics**: the
    payload defines room-list *membership* (rooms not listed are removed),
    but a payload room whose `name` matches an existing room **merges
    field-wise** into it (via `Room::processJsonAsObj(install)`, with the
    `name` key stripped so mere matching doesn't force a relaunch). Unknown
    fields of an existing room are preserved; new names create rooms;
    entries without `name` are ignored with a warning.
  - Per-parameter changes remain `cmd/<room-location>/set` (pure field merge,
    no membership effect) — this is also what `thermoctl set` now uses.
  - After the rebuild, `Thermo::subscribe()` re-registers the device-level
    routes (skipped on the `Level::load` boot path where setup registers
    them); the redundant `resubscribeAll()` is dropped since every kept/new
    room re-subscribes explicitly.
  - `doc/MQTT.md` updated to document these semantics and the install-level
    reboot rule.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - [x] Partial device-level rooms-set merges fields; unspecified fields and
        unlisted... rooms listed by name keep all unspecified fields (verified
        by `thermoctl test` check `f.devset.merge` on GIMYB)
  - [x] Membership semantics: rooms omitted from the payload are removed,
        new names created (`f.devset.membership`)
  - [x] `cmd/<id>/get` still answered after a rooms-set (`f.devset.routes`,
        regression for Bug B)
  - [x] Boot path unchanged: stored config loads, no duplicate device routes
  - [x] `doc/MQTT.md` documents deployment vs. per-room set semantics
  - [x] Full `thermoctl test --suite functional` passes on GIMYB with the fix
- **Notes:**
  - Legacy 0.6.4 fleet devices keep Bug A: never send partial device-level
    rooms-sets to them. `thermoctl set` uses room-topic sets, which are safe
    on all firmware versions.
  - Incident record: 7ROBA clobbered + restored 2026-07-04 (see REQ-027
    session); restoration source was the thermoctl survey inventory cache.
